title: Pocket Atlas
tagline: Cozy pixel puzzles for learning, or re-learning, how computers really work.
intro: Pocket Atlas turns big technical subjects into small places you can walk around. Each subject is a region on the atlas, with its own map, its own story and short puzzle levels of about 3 to 8 minutes.
It's free, it needs no account, and it runs in your browser. Your stars are saved on this device only.
who: Curious people who have never studied the subject and want a gentle way in.
Students who met these ideas once and want to refresh them without opening a textbook.
Anyone who learns better by doing a puzzle than by reading a page.
howIntro: Every level follows the same short path, so you always know what's next.

how.name: A question from real life
how.text: Each level starts with something you have probably wondered about, like why undo works the way it does.

how.name: A short story and the key ideas
how.text: A small story in the region sets the scene, then a few plain-language points give you what you need.

how.name: Puzzles
how.text: You try the idea hands-on. Wrong answers give you a hint, never a penalty timer.

how.name: Debrief
how.text: You get the answer to the opening question, a common mistake to avoid, your stars and links to read more.

extras.name: Daily Feed
extras.text: About 10 bite-size review cards a day from levels you've finished. Cards you miss come back sooner. There's a streak, but it never scolds you.

extras.name: Field Journal
extras.text: Every finished level unlocks Field Notes: where the idea shows up in the apps and networks you use today.

subjectsIntro: Each region keeps its own progress. Start anywhere.
progress: {earned} of {max} stars in the {levels} built so far
note: All explanations, stories and puzzles are original. The reading links at the end of each level point to open books, official specs and other sources.
